survivors.title: `converged` only inspects the last k agent steps of ANY tool name, so padding the cycle with k clean throwaway steps forces green.
survivors.anchor: .claude/skills/dev-loop/qa_ledger.py:635-642
survivors.scenario: `agent = [all agent-category steps]`; `last_cycle = agent[-k:]`. Tool identity is never checked — there is no requirement that the last k steps cover the k distinct tools in qa_tools_order. With k=3, after a dirty real cycle the agent logs three more steps `log-step --tool code-review --reported 0 --gated-reported 0 --files-changed 0 --tests-passed true` (same tool, or any names). `last_cycle` is now those 3 clean rows, `gated`=0, `changed`=0, tests green -> CONVERGED. The prior dirty findings are simply pushed out of the `[-k:]` window.
survivors.fix: Require the last cycle to contain one step per DISTINCT tool in `config.defaults.qa_tools_order` (validate the set of tool names in `last_cycle`), and treat any tool that reported gated>0 in a *later-superseded* step as still-open until a real re-run of THAT tool clears it. Convergence should be 'every tool's latest run is clean', mirroring the static-gate logic at :649-650, not 'the trailing k rows are clean'.
survivors.fix_note: Fix is directionally right but over-corrects/adds redundant ceremony. Part A (require last cycle to cover each distinct tool in qa_tools_order) is a cheap, correct hardening that mirrors the static half. Part B ("treat any tool with gated>0 in a later-superseded step as still-open until a real re-run of THAT tool clears it") reinvents state that _latest_static_by_tool / _gate_open_and_sev already provide for the scored gate; its own stated end-goal ("every tool's latest run is clean") is exactly latest-per-tool. Minimal fix: change the agent half of _converged to iterate the latest agent step PER TOOL in qa_tools_order (symmetric with _latest_static_by_tool at lines 649-650) and require all listed tools present — no new superseded-tracking bookkeeping needed. Also note the framing error: convergence is advisory and readiness's BLOCKER/CRITICAL/tests caps already run latest-per-tool, so no fix is needed to prevent the KPI from being forced green — only the advisory signal and conv_dim need the symmetry fix.

survivors.title: `check-coverage` treats a present-but-tiny/stale JaCoCo report as authoritative, so shrinking the measured surface passes the coverage gate without new tests.
survivors.anchor: .claude/skills/dev-loop/qa_ledger.py:472-490 ; :106-140
survivors.scenario: `_jacoco_line_counter` returns the report-level LINE counter and `maven_coverage` computes pct = covered/(covered+missed) purely from whatever jacoco.xml exists. There is no check that the report covers the production classes, that it is fresh, or that `total` is non-trivial. A dev configures JaCoCo `<excludes>` to drop the hard-to-test packages, or runs coverage over a single trivial module — pct jumps above threshold with the same tests. Worse: a report with covered=1, missed=0 yields 100%. `report_found` is `bool(files)`, so any jacoco.xml (even from an unrelated/old module) flips the gate from BELOW to OK.
survivors.fix: Record and gate on the absolute `total` (covered+missed) lines and compare against the prod LOC from `count_loc`; flag when measured total collapses vs the prior snapshot (a shrinking denominator is a regression signal). Reject a report whose total is implausibly small relative to prod_loc, and warn on JaCoCo excludes if detectable.
survivors.fix_note: Partly redundant, partly over-correcting. The snapshot ALREADY records prod_loc per snapshot (_snapshot :442-453) and config has rebuild.coverage_tolerance:5, so the denominator is already tracked pre/post — the fix's "flag when measured total collapses vs prior snapshot" is the one genuinely additive, reasonable hardening. But "reject a report whose total is implausibly small relative to prod_loc from count_loc" over-corrects: JaCoCo LINE counters instrument bytecode lines, whereas count_loc counts non-blank source lines — different units with a legitimately variable ratio (interfaces, DTOs, records, generated code), so a hard rejection risks false-blocking valid reports (ceremony that is itself a weakness). "Warn on JaCoCo excludes if detectable" is speculative: excludes live in pom/plugin config that jacoco.xml does not emit, so it is largely undetectable from the report the code parses. Minimal sound change: add a freshness/mtime check and a soft WARN (not a hard reject) when covered+missed collapses vs the prior snapshot's total or is trivially small.

survivors.title: pit-check gates on `mutation_score = killed/total` while NO_COVERAGE mutants count in `total`, but the real dodge is scoping PIT's targetClasses — either way survivors are hidden.
survivors.anchor: .claude/skills/dev-loop/qa_ledger.py:1540-1571 ; :1587
survivors.scenario: The gate is `m['mutation_score'] >= min_score` where mutation_score = killed/total (:1567,:1587). PIT only mutates the classes its Maven config points at. A dev narrows `<targetClasses>`/`<targetTests>` to the well-tested package; PIT generates few mutants, nearly all killed, score ~100 — the untested code is simply never mutated and never appears in the denominator. The engine cannot see what PIT chose not to mutate. Separately, because the *conventional* score counts NO_COVERAGE mutants as unkilled in `total`, a genuinely improving suite can still read BELOW-GATE while `test_strength` (killed/covered, :1569) is high — so a lazy dev is nudged to shrink scope rather than add asserts.
survivors.fix: Emit and gate on mutated-class count vs `count_loc` prod_files (or vs the JaCoCo class list); fail or warn when PIT's covered surface is materially smaller than the production surface. Consider gating on `test_strength` for scope-robustness and separately flag `no_coverage>0` as a coverage-gap that must not be closed by shrinking targetClasses.
survivors.fix_note: The fix is partly redundant, partly harmful, and partly over-correcting. (a) "Flag no_coverage>0 as a coverage-gap distinct from assertion-gap" is ALREADY implemented at :1613-1615 and :1607-1610 — pure ceremony. (b) "Gate on test_strength for scope-robustness" is actively wrong: test_strength = killed/covered (:1569) EXCLUDES uncovered code from the denominator, so gating on it makes the tool blind to coverage gaps and REWARDS the narrowing dodge — the opposite of the stated goal. (c) The one genuinely-new idea — emit mutated-class count vs prod surface and warn when PIT's covered surface is materially smaller than production — is a legitimate hardening against Prong 1, but it over-corrects: the methodology deliberately measures effectiveness only "en el área tocada" (CONSTITUTION:54) and tiers PIT as scheduled/incremental, not inner-loop (:94), so a whole-repo surface comparison would false-positive on every intentionally-scoped run. A minimal, sound version would be a SEPARATE scoped warning (e.g. detect narrowing of PIT targetClasses under gate-check's "don't weaken the measurer" umbrella) rather than gating pit-check on test_strength or on a repo-wide surface diff.

survivors.title: gate-check's threshold-lowering detector requires the old and new number to sit on adjacent -/+ lines with matching keywords, so a reformatted or split edit evades it entirely.
survivors.anchor: .claude/skills/dev-loop/qa_ledger.py:1680-1686 ; :1658 (last_removed reset)
survivors.scenario: `thresholds` only fires when a `+` line matches `_GC_CONFIG` path AND `_GC_THRESH` AND `last_removed` (the immediately-preceding `-` line) also matches `_GC_THRESH` and `float(new[0]) < float(old[0])`. `last_removed` is reset to None on any context line and after every `+` (:1686). So to lower coverage from 60 to 30 without a BLOCKER: (a) put an unrelated context/comment line between the removed and added line, (b) move the number to a different line than the keyword (`<minimum>\n  30</minimum>` split), (c) change it in a file whose name doesn't match `_GC_CONFIG` (e.g. a custom `quality.properties` or a shell script that exports the threshold), or (d) delete the whole config block in one hunk and re-add a new one in a later hunk (removed line no longer adjacent). `--from-git` uses `--unified=0` (:1289) which removes context lines but any reformatting still breaks adjacency.
survivors.fix: Parse config files structurally (key -> numeric value) before/after rather than line-adjacency matching; compare threshold KEYS across the whole diff, not adjacent -/+ pairs. Broaden `_GC_CONFIG` to any file the config actually reads (dev-loop.config.json is covered, but sonar/quality props via variables are not), and flag deletion of a threshold key without re-add.
survivors.fix_note: The fix's CORE is minimal and correct: track any removed `_GC_THRESH` line's key+number and match it against any added `_GC_THRESH` line for the SAME file across all hunks (not just the adjacent `-`), plus flag deletion of a threshold key with no re-add. That kills scenarios (a), (b), (d) in a handful of stdlib lines and stays within the tool's diff-only contract. However two of the four proposed parts OVER-CORRECT: (1) "parse config files structurally (key->numeric) before/after" expands gate-check from a format-agnostic diff scanner into a per-format (JSON/XML/gradle/properties) parser that must reconstruct both file versions or read the working tree — significant ceremony for a heuristic tool; and (3) broadening `_GC_CONFIG` to "any file the config actually reads" including sonar/quality props via shell variables is unbounded and invites false positives on unrelated numeric edits (which would themselves become a weakness, since false BLOCKERs erode trust in the fact-gate). Recommend adopting only the cross-hunk key-matching + deletion-without-readd checks; skip full structural parsing and open-ended path broadening. Scenario (c) — thresholds in a file entirely outside `_GC_CONFIG` — is a real gap but is better closed by adding the SPECIFIC extra config globs the kit uses (sonar-project.properties is already covered) than by an unbounded broadening.

survivors.title: gate-check's test-removal detection is keyed on filename/path heuristics, so moving deletions into a non-matching file (or renaming) lets tests vanish without a BLOCKER.
survivors.anchor: .claude/skills/dev-loop/qa_ledger.py:1642-1649 ; :1689-1691
survivors.scenario: `removed_tests`/`assertions_removed` only accrue when `_gc_is_test_file(path)` is true — i.e. path contains /test/ or basename ends with e.g. `Test.java`/`_test.py`. A dev deletes real tests by first renaming the file to something outside the heuristic (e.g. `FooChecks.java` in a `support/` dir the build still runs), or gutting a helper that tests delegate to (helper isn't a test file, so removed assertions there aren't counted), or deleting an entire test file via `diff --git ... /dev/null` where the `+++` is `/dev/null` -> path set to None (:1669) -> the whole file's removed `@Test` lines are skipped because `if not path: continue` (:1671). Deleting a test file wholesale therefore reports CLEAN.
survivors.fix: When `+++` is /dev/null, capture the file identity from the `--- a/...` line and still evaluate removed `@Test`/assert lines against it. Detect test-file DELETIONS (git `deleted file mode` / rename) as a hard signal, and cross-check the post-change test COUNT (surefire totals) against baseline — a drop in executed tests is a fact the ledger already can measure.
survivors.fix_note: Sound and minimal, not over-correcting — and more faithful to the method's "measure facts" ethos than the current code. Part (a) recovering file identity from `--- a/...` on `+++ /dev/null` is a few lines in the existing loop and closes the dominant hole. Part (c) — cross-checking the executed test COUNT against baseline — is the strongest heuristic-independent defense and adds NO new machinery: the kit already computes this exact fact (maven_test_count at :170; rebuild --mode compare flags a total-count drop at :1207-1211 "fewer behaviors exercised"). The real defect is that this fact lives in the optional Phase-5b `rebuild compare` subcommand, not wired into the inner-loop gate-check. Part (b) (deleted-file-mode/rename hard signal) is partly redundant with (a) and carries a minor false-positive risk (a legitimately deleted non-test file must still be filtered through test-file logic before blocking), but (a) already handles that. Net: adopt (a)+(c) primarily.

survivors.title: Static-gate convergence trusts ingested reports but an ABSENT report is 'last state stands', so deleting/not-running a linter freezes a stale-clean gated_open forever.
survivors.anchor: .claude/skills/dev-loop/qa_ledger.py:578-580 ; :624-655 ; :835-843
survivors.scenario: `ingest-gate` only seeds a zero step for tools whose report FILE existed this run (`present`, :551-563); an absent report is intentionally NOT treated as clean and its last state stands (comment :576-578). Combined with `_latest_static_by_tool` (last wins), the move is: on the cycle where SpotBugs would flag security bugs, simply don't produce `spotbugsXml.xml` (remove the plugin exec, or point it at an empty source set). ingest-gate finds no SpotBugs file, logs nothing for it, and `_gate_open_and_sev` uses the LAST spotbugs step — which, if the tool never ran a dirty pass, is absent or an old clean one. `static_dim` and convergence then see zero gated_open. The engine explicitly refuses to penalize a linter that 'didn't run', so not-running it is strictly better than running it dirty.
survivors.fix: Convergence/readiness must require that the EXPECTED linter set (from config) all have a fresh report in the current iteration; a linter with no report in the current iteration should block convergence ('gate did not run'), not inherit an old clean state. Track expected-vs-present tools per iteration and treat missing-expected as NOT converged.
survivors.fix_note: The fix's CORE INSIGHT is right (track expected-vs-present linters per iteration), but its prescription over-corrects and adds ceremony. (1) The config has no expected-linter set — adding one is new required config across every repo, and per-repo (Flutter mobile-app has no Checkstyle/PMD/SpotBugs at all, so a global expected set would hard-block Flutter convergence forever). (2) Requiring a FRESH report in the CURRENT iteration punishes legitimate incremental cycles: a later cycle that only re-runs the agent tools (SpotBugs unchanged, not re-emitted) would be marked NOT converged — the "last state stands" design exists precisely to avoid re-running every linter every cycle. (3) It converts an explicitly-advisory signal into a hard block, contradicting the method's advisory design. A minimal, philosophy-consistent fix: track expected-vs-present and SURFACE the gap loudly in readiness/converged output ("spotbugs: no report this iteration — gate did not run") as an advisory downgrade, plus have ingest-gate warn on a missing subset (not only zero reports) — no new hard-freshness block, no per-repo expected-set ceremony that breaks Flutter.

survivors.title: readiness hard caps only trip on data the agent controls, so the BLOCKER/CRITICAL and tests-red caps are trivially avoided by not reporting them.
survivors.anchor: .claude/skills/dev-loop/qa_ledger.py:967-977 ; :846-856 ; :888-890
survivors.scenario: The `blocker_critical` cap (<=65) reads `agg_sev` from `severity_counts` on static-gate steps (:970, :839-842) — which only exist if the linter report was ingested (see prior finding). Don't ingest -> no BLOCKER/CRITICAL severity counts -> cap never trips. The `tests_red` cap (:968, :846-856) reads either the last snapshot's failures/errors OR the last agent step's `tests_passed`; the agent supplies `--tests-passed true` and never takes a failing snapshot, so `_tests_red` is False. The `escalation` cap (:973) only trips if the agent called `escalate` at all. Every hard cap depends on the agent voluntarily surfacing the bad state; a lazy agent that logs only green never trips any cap and readiness is free to hit READY (>=95).
survivors.fix: Compute tests-red from a freshly parsed surefire/failsafe report taken by the engine (snapshot) at readiness time, not from `--tests-passed`; compute BLOCKER/CRITICAL from the current-iteration ingested reports and treat 'expected linter missing' as an automatic cap rather than absence-of-evidence.
survivors.fix_note: The proposed fix over-corrects and adds ceremony while duplicating existing machinery. (1) "Compute tests-red from a freshly parsed surefire report taken by the engine at readiness time": the engine ALREADY parses surefire/failsafe XML in `_snapshot`/`maven_test_count`, and SKILL.md:185 mandates a post snapshot before readiness. The gap is not a missing parser — it's that `_tests_red` prefers the snapshot only when present. A minimal fix would be to make readiness REFUSE (or auto-cap) when no post-snapshot exists for a repo, rather than adding a second independent surefire parse inside cmd_readiness (duplicated I/O, two code paths that can disagree). (2) "Treat 'expected linter missing' as an automatic cap rather than absence-of-evidence" is the RIGHT direction but is really the prior separate finding (absence=clean on static_gate:941 scoring 1.0 and severity path). Folding it in here conflates two findings. (3) Crucially, the fix aims at an outcome (agent games READY) that the engine-observed coverage floor already prevents (max 72.2 without a real report), so the additional readiness-time surefire re-parse buys little for the stated threat. The honest minimal change is: gate readiness on presence of a post-snapshot + coverage report per repo (fail-closed on absence), reusing existing parsers — not adding a fresh parse plus new automatic caps.

survivors.title: The golden-diff / block-approved-writes invariant is bypassable: the agent can make a failing golden pass by editing the .received (or the comparison inputs), which the hook does not protect.
survivors.anchor: hooks/block-approved-writes.ps1:22-34 ; qa_ledger.py:1911-1929
survivors.scenario: The hook blocks writes/renames to `*.approved*` only. golden-diff passes when `rb == ab` (received bytes == approved bytes, :1926). The agent cannot touch .approved — but it CAN write the `.received` file (not blocked) to exactly equal the approved content, or regenerate the capture with the assertion neutered so the received output matches. Nothing verifies the .received was produced by an unmodified capture path. Also, the Bash matcher (:29-30) only blocks .approved writes that co-occur with a redirect/mv/cp keyword on the same command; `printf ... | tee $f` where $f is a variable holding the .approved path, or a python one-liner `open(p,'w')`, is not matched (no `>`/`tee`/`cp`/etc. token OR the path is indirected through a var).
survivors.fix: Have the capture harness (not the agent) write .received to a location the agent can't write, or checksum the capture command. Strengthen the hook: block any Bash command referencing a `.approved` path regardless of accompanying keyword, and resolve variable/indirect targets, or move enforcement to a filesystem ACL rather than a command-string regex.
survivors.fix_note: Half-sound, half over-correcting. The minimal correct fix for the confirmed hole (B) is exactly one line: drop the second regex and block ANY Bash command whose string references a .approved path (hook:29-30 -> `if ($cmd -match '\.approved') { $block = $true }`). False-positive cost is trivial — golden files are binary (.gitattributes `*.approved.* binary`, characterize:71) and the agent has no legitimate reason to touch an .approved path via Bash; it can still Read via the Read tool. That closes open()/dd/write_text with zero ceremony. The rest of the proposed fix OVER-CORRECTS and adds ceremony aimed at sub-claim A (out of scope): (1) "checksum the capture command" does not even prevent hand-writing .received and adds a verification layer for a threat the invariant doesn't own; (2) "harness writes .received to a location the agent can't write" and "filesystem ACLs instead of a regex" are heavy operational infrastructure for a solo dev-loop kit, defending the wrong threat. "Resolve variable/indirect targets" in a PreToolUse regex is also infeasible (you'd need to execute the shell to resolve $f) — the blanket-block obviates it. Recommend: apply only the one-line broadening; discard the ACL/checksum/harness-relocation additions.

survivors.title: Oscillation detection is period-2 fingerprint equality and requires the agent to supply --fingerprint, so it is off-by-default and defeated by a one-line churn.
survivors.anchor: .claude/skills/dev-loop/qa_ledger.py:683-692 ; :503-505
survivors.scenario: `fps` is built only from steps where the agent passed `--fingerprint` (fingerprint is None otherwise, :519). If the agent never passes fingerprints, oscillation exits 2 ('cannot judge') and the loop proceeds — the SKILL's escalation trigger 'oscillation detected' never fires. Even when fingerprints are given, detection is strictly `fps[-1] == fps[-3]` (period 2). An agent stuck fixing-and-reintroducing the same finding just needs the fingerprint SET to differ by one ID each pass (touch a trivial nearby line so one finding-ID shifts), making fps[-1] != fps[-3] though the substantive finding recurs. Period-3+ oscillation is invisible by construction.
survivors.fix: Make fingerprints mandatory for agent QA steps (derive them from finding-IDs like ingest-gate does, not a free CLI arg), detect recurrence by set-overlap/Jaccard over a window rather than exact period-2 equality, and treat 'no fingerprints' as a blocking condition, not exit-2 'cannot judge'.
survivors.fix_note: Two of three fix elements are sound and proportionate; the third over-corrects and contradicts the method's own constitution. SOUND: (a) auto-deriving fingerprints from finding-IDs — ingest-gate already does this at :597, so it is proven low-ceremony and closes both the off-by-default gap and the maker==checker coupling; (b) set-overlap/Jaccard over a window instead of exact period-2 — adds a window/threshold param (moderate machinery) but proportionate to a genuinely brittle exact-hash-equality check. OVER-CORRECTS: treating "no fingerprints" as a BLOCKING condition instead of exit-2. Oscillation is explicitly ADVISORY (docstring :677, SKILL :156 "advisory — you make the final call"); the method's core principle is "guesses may only advise." Converting a missing advisory heuristic into a hard block turns a guess into a blocker — the exact thing the constitution forbids. And once fingerprints are auto-derived (element a), the "no fingerprints" case largely vanishes for agent steps, making the block both unnecessary and self-contradictory. Drop element 3; keep 1 and a bounded version of 2.

survivors.title: simplicity-check counts only files matching a source-extension allowlist and skips 'noise' dirs, so moving bulk into skipped files or non-listed extensions dodges the OVERBUILT cap.
survivors.anchor: .claude/skills/dev-loop/qa_ledger.py:1080-1084 ; :1320-1330 ; :1362-1367
survivors.scenario: `_is_simplicity_code_file` returns False for any path with a segment in `_SIMPLICITY_SKIP` or whose extension isn't in `_SIMPLICITY_CODE_EXT`. lines_added/files_changed/max_hunk only accrue for counting files (:1371-1375). An overbuilt change can be parked in a `generated-sources/` path, in `.xml`/`.yaml`/`.properties`/`.sql`/`.ftl`/`.mustache` templates, or in a language not on the list — all invisible to the budget. The hard cap (:1427-1435) is computed from the same filtered metrics, so a 5000-line addition entirely in resources/config scores SIMPLE. Since Phase 2b treats OVERBUILT as a BLOCKER but SIMPLE/ACCEPTABLE as pass, relocating complexity into non-code files sails through.
survivors.fix: At least COUNT total added lines across all changed files (even if only code files feed the nesting/abstraction proxies) and flag when skipped-file additions dwarf code additions. Include common template/resource-with-logic extensions, and warn when a large fraction of the diff lands in skipped paths.
survivors.fix_note: The fix is split. Its ADVISORY half is sound and method-consistent: adding a lines_skipped total plus a "most of the diff landed in non-code paths" flag is cheap and matches the existing files_skipped surfacing (:1390, :1506-1507) and the "guesses may only advise" pattern. Its BLOCKING half over-corrects: making total-added-lines (including .sql/.xml/.xsd/.yaml) feed the OVERBUILT band or hard cap would turn honest resource additions (Flyway migrations, generated WSDL/XSD, golden-master fixtures — all committed in this repo) into false blockers, adding exactly the false-positive ceremony the gate deliberately avoids by scoping to code. Recommend implementing only as an advisory flag, not a gate input. Note the "include template/resource-with-logic extensions" suggestion is ambiguous (.ftl/.mustache/.sql have no honest nesting/abstraction proxy) and would degrade the code-only invariant.

survivors.title: rebuild 'tests' dimension is gamed by shrinking or trivializing the preserved suite, because the compare is ratio-based (rebuilt/baseline) and only the baseline count is captured.
survivors.anchor: .claude/skills/dev-loop/qa_ledger.py:1197-1211 ; :1127-1144
survivors.scenario: tests_dim when green = `min(1.0, t1_total / t0_total)` (:1207-1208). The baseline signature captures only totals/passed and the test_file_set (:1142), not per-test identity or assertions. To score COVERS after a divergent rebuild, the agent preserves the test FILES (so the file-set matches) but the passing count just needs to reach the baseline total — it can neuter assertions inside preserved tests (they still 'pass'), or the rebuilt tree can include extra trivial passing tests to lift t1_total. Because failures/errors dominate only when >0 (:1202), a suite of assertion-free tests yields tests_dim=1.0. The 'preserved suite' is validated by count and filename, never by content hash.
survivors.fix: Hash each preserved test file in the baseline and verify byte-identity of the test_file_set on compare (reuse the golden-diff philosophy); reject the run if any preserved test file changed. Gate tests_dim on per-test pass identity, not aggregate totals.
survivors.fix_note: Over-corrects and adds ceremony. Byte-identity hashing + reject-on-any-change is too strict: legitimate rebuilds touch test files for import/namespace churn (this very project's javax->jakarta migration) and fixture moves, producing constant false DIVERGE and violating the method's own 'facts may block; guesses may only advise' — a formatting diff is not a divergence fact. 'Per-test pass identity' demands cross-framework per-test parsing (pytest/junit/go/jest), heavy surface the deliberately-tiny 4-line ratio avoids, for an optional periodic gate. The MINIMAL fix reuses data already captured: compare sig0['test_file_set'] vs sig1['test_file_set'] as SET MEMBERSHIP and emit a gap/advisory (not a hard reject) when preserved files go missing — matching 'guesses may only advise'. The proposed hash-and-reject is a heavier hammer than the hole warrants.

survivors.title: spec-check is advisory-by-default and its testability/EARS checks are keyword regexes, so a vague spec passes and even --strict is satisfied by inserting a bare number or measurable-looking token.
survivors.anchor: .claude/skills/dev-loop/qa_ledger.py:1824 ; :1858-1860 ; :1754-1758
survivors.scenario: `untestable` = criteria matching `_SC_VAGUE` AND NOT `_SC_MEASURABLE` (:1824). To clear a vague criterion the author appends any `_SC_MEASURABLE` token — e.g. 'the UI should be user-friendly within 500ms' — the `500ms` makes it 'measurable' though the assertion is still 'user-friendly'. Structure blockers only require the literal presence of an out-of-scope heading and any acceptance section with >=1 non-empty item (:1827-1830); a one-line '- [ ] works' under an 'Acceptance' heading plus an empty 'Non-goals' heading satisfies both. And since the whole command is advisory unless `--strict` (:1859), by default n_find>0 still exits 0.
survivors.fix: This one is inherently inferential (the doc even says consistency is a non-correlated-checker job), so keep it advisory but stop letting a co-located measurable token exempt a vague clause — require the measurable to bind the SAME predicate, or downgrade to 'still flagged'. Consider making --strict the default in the SKILL's Phase 0 so at least structure blockers gate.
survivors.fix_note: The fix splits cleanly into two parts with different quality. PART 1 (predicate-binding / downgrade) is SOUND and aligned with the method's own standard. The tool explicitly frames itself as COMPUTATIONAL testability proxies, not inferential consistency (lines 1739-1744), and the author already anticipated a nearby bypass (bare-digit, line 1752). The proposed "require the measurable to bind the SAME predicate" is genuinely inferential (proximity/dependency parsing over prose is exactly the guessing the method says belongs to the non-correlated checker), so the SAFER and non-over-correcting variant the fix also offers — "downgrade to still-flagged" rather than exempt — is the right call: keep it advisory, but stop the co-located token from silently clearing the vague clause. That is minimal and honest (a guess advises, it does not exempt-and-hide). PART 2 ("make --strict the default in Phase 0 so structure blockers gate") OVER-CORRECTS and rests on a false premise: spec-check is NOT invoked in Phase 0 or anywhere in the SKILLs (verified: zero references in dev-loop/adr-refine). There is no Phase 0 call to flip. Wiring a strict-by-default spec gate into the flow would (a) contradict the method's core "facts may block; guesses may only advise" principle by promoting a keyword-regex heuristic to a blocker, and (b) add ceremony — the structure blockers are themselves trivially game-able (empty headings satisfy them), so gating on them buys little and would generate false-blocks on legitimately-phrased specs. Recommendation: adopt Part 1's downgrade variant only; drop Part 2. Net: the fix is directionally correct but its second half should be discarded as over-correction/ceremony.

survivors.title: Readiness weights line coverage at 25/100 and never ingests mutation score, so the headline KPI enshrines the exact 'coverage lies' trap the CONSTITUTION forbids.
survivors.anchor: qa_ledger.py:873-874 (cov_dim = cov['pct']) and :959-964 (dims has no mutation term); pit-check isolated at :1574-1616 with zero readiness callers (grep confirms no reference in cmd_readiness)
survivors.scenario: A repo has 60% line coverage produced by tests with no assertions (execute-but-don't-verify). readiness: cov_dim = min(60/60,1.0)=1.0 → full 25 points. mutation_score could be 5% and readiness never sees it because pit-check output is never fed into the ledger or the score. The system reports RELEASE CANDIDATE / READY while its tests catch nothing. CONSTITUTION.md:47-56 explicitly states 'coverage miente ... coverage alto con mutantes vivos = falsa seguridad' — the primary KPI contradicts the project's own inviolable invariant.
survivors.fix: Either (a) make pit-check write a static-gate-style step into the ledger and add a 'test_effectiveness' dimension to readiness fed by mutation_score, or (b) demote line-coverage's weight and stop labeling a 60%-line-coverage repo as full-credit on 'coverage'. At minimum, cap readiness (like tests_red) when a mutation report exists and is below --min-score.
survivors.fix_note: Fix (a) over-corrects: adding a weighted test_effectiveness dimension fed by mutation_score forces PIT (expensive full mutation run) into every readiness call and has no sane value when no mutations.xml exists (0 would tank every repo that hasn't run PIT; a neutral default would re-open the same blindness). Weight-demotion is also unnecessary given coverage is already only 25 of a capped composite. The sound, minimal part is the claim's own "at minimum" clause: add a conditional cap in _apply_caps that fires ONLY when a mutation report exists and mutation_score < --min-score, mirroring the existing tests_red/blocker_critical cap pattern. That is faithful to "facts may block": a present-and-failing PIT report is a fact and blocks; its absence advises nothing and adds no ceremony. Secondary low-cost fix: document the pit-check->CONSTITUTION-breach->BLOCKER path in the readiness section so the manual wiring isn't silently skippable.

survivors.title: Static-gate dimension (20 pts) and convergence dimension (15 pts) default to a PERFECT score when the gate/tools were simply never run — silence is scored as success.
survivors.anchor: qa_ledger.py:835-843 (_gate_open_and_sev returns gated_open=0 when latest={} i.e. no static-gate steps) → :941 static_dim=1.0; and :632-655 _converged: 'gated' sums default to 0 for a clean cycle, so a repo with exactly k trivial agent steps and no static-gate steps converges
survivors.scenario: Agent runs Phase 3 but skips `ingest-gate` (or the java-qa-gate never emits XML). readiness: total_open=0 → static_dim=1.0 → full 20 points for a linter suite that never executed. Combined with a passing (assertion-free) suite and a few logged log-step calls with gated=0/files_changed=0, static(20)+convergence(15)+coverage(25) all award full marks. The score reflects absence of measurement, not absence of defects. The SKILL comment at :576-578 correctly says an ABSENT report 'is NOT treated as clean' for convergence's fix-crediting, but readiness's static_dim still treats total_open==0 identically whether the gate ran clean or never ran.
survivors.fix: Track per-linter 'report_found' presence in the ledger and make static_dim=0 (or cap the score / mark UNMEASURED) when no static-gate step exists for a repo, instead of defaulting gated_open=0 → 1.0. Same for convergence: distinguish 'converged' from 'never measured'.
survivors.fix_note: Direction is correct and minimal — distinguish 'never measured' from 'clean', mirroring the already-present integration pattern (integ_dim=0.0 when required-but-never-run, :954-955). The proposed 'track per-linter report_found in the ledger' is slightly heavier than needed: the ledger already encodes presence implicitly (`_latest_static_by_tool` returns {} when none ran), and readiness already knows repo type (:872) and the configured repo list, so the fix can be a small branch (lint-capable repo with empty latest → static_dim=0.0 or UNMEASURED) without a new persisted field. Marking UNMEASURED / capping rather than a hard 0.0 is preferable so a repo with genuinely no lint config isn't unfairly penalized — but that is config-driven, not ceremony. No meaningful over-correction.

survivors.title: Rebuild-test 'tests' dimension (60% weight) rewards test COUNT ratio, not behavioral equivalence — a rebuilt tree that keeps the files but silently weakens tests scores COVERS.
survivors.anchor: qa_ledger.py:1206-1211 (tests_dim = min(1.0, t1['total']/t0['total']) when zero failures) and :1112-1124 _test_file_set only records file paths, never content hashes
survivors.scenario: Baseline has 200 passing tests. Rebuild preserves the same test files but the agent (or a merge) turned 50 of them into no-op/assertion-stripped tests that still 'pass'. t1.total=200, t1.failures=0 → ratio=1.0 → tests_dim=1.0 → 60/60 of the dominant weight. Verdict COVERS at ~100. The rebuild test's stated dominant signal ('tests that passed originally but fail on regenerated code') is defeated because a preserved-but-gutted test passes trivially. The doc claims the preserved suite is the guardrail, but the metric only checks it still passes and still numerically exists — never that it still asserts the same behavior. gate-check (which detects assertion removal) is a separate command not wired into rebuild.
survivors.fix: In baseline, store a per-test-file content hash / assertion count alongside test_file_set; in compare, flag files whose assertion density dropped or whose content changed, and dock tests_dim. Or run pit-check on the rebuilt tree and factor test_strength into the tests dimension.
survivors.fix_note: The primary proposed fix is sound and minimal: store a per-test-file assertion count (or content hash) alongside the already-collected test_file_set in _repo_signature, then in _rebuild_compare flag files whose assertion density dropped and dock tests_dim. This reuses existing machinery (the test_file_set walk and the _GC_ASSERT regex already present at line 1633) — no new heavy dependency, low ceremony, closes the exact hole. The SECONDARY variant (run pit-check/mutation testing on the rebuilt tree and factor test_strength in) WOULD over-correct: mutation testing is expensive and slow, disproportionate for a coarse completeness gate that otherwise runs on cheap static signatures. So take the assertion-count/hash variant, not the pit-check variant. One caveat to keep it minimal: a content-hash comparison alone would false-positive on legitimate test reformatting during rebuild; an assertion-COUNT (or density) drop is the more robust signal and should be preferred over raw hash equality.

survivors.title: Simplicity score is defeatable: seven independent linear-decay dims mean a diff can be ~1.9x over budget on the heavy dimensions and still land ACCEPTABLE, and the only hard cap fires at 2x.
survivors.anchor: qa_ledger.py:1402-1408 (_adherence: linear to 0 at 2x budget), :1411-1436 (weights diff_size35/nesting30/net20; crit cap only at >2x budget or nesting+3), :1067 SIMPLICITY_BANDS ACCEPTABLE floor 65
survivors.scenario: A change adds 780 lines (budget 400, 1.95x → diff_size adherence≈0.05) but is otherwise tidy: nesting=4 (1.0), net_lines under 300 if it also deletes a lot, files=20 (1.0), hunks under 120 (1.0), no new types (1.0). Weighted: 35*0.05 + 30*1.0 + 20*1.0 + 8*1.0 + 7*1.0 = 1.75+65 = ~66.75/100 → ACCEPTABLE (passes the OVERBUILT gate, exit 0). The 'crit' hard cap (:1427-1433) does not fire because 780 < 2*400. So a diff nearly double the added-lines budget passes the simplicity gate as long as the cheap-to-satisfy structural dims are clean. The proxy is honest about what it measures but the aggregation lets a gross size overrun be masked by trivially-green secondary dims — the exact masking the :1426 comment claims to prevent, which it only prevents past 2x.
survivors.fix: Make diff_size/net_lines decay steeper (0 at 1.5x, not 2x) or lower the crit-cap trigger to 1.5x for the size dims; alternatively require ALL heavy dims (diff_size, net_growth) above a floor for a SIMPLE/ACCEPTABLE verdict rather than letting the weighted sum average them away.
survivors.fix_note: The proposed 'require ALL heavy dims (diff_size, net_growth) above a floor rather than letting the weighted sum average them away' is the sound, minimal, non-ceremonial option and I'd prefer it over the other two alternatives. It has direct in-codebase precedent: the abstraction dimension already uses min() of two _adherence values (qa_ledger.py:1416-1419) instead of contributing to the weighted average, precisely to prevent one clean sub-metric from masking the other. Applying the same min()-floor discipline to diff_size/net_growth is consistent with the existing design and adds no magic constants. The 'decay to 0 at 1.5x' alternative introduces an arbitrary constant and would also penalize legitimate 1.2-1.4x diffs harder across the board (over-correction risk); 'lower crit-cap to 1.5x for size dims' is a narrower magic-number tweak that works but is less principled than the floor approach. Recommend the floor-on-heavy-dims variant. Keep the flag output as-is (it already surfaces the fact); the change needed is only that the verdict must not reach SIMPLE/ACCEPTABLE while a heavy dim is below floor.

survivors.title: The readiness KPI's heaviest dimension (ADR=30) silently zeroes out because SKILL.md tells you to pass a --section that the shipped ACCEPTANCE.md template does not contain
survivors.anchor: qa_ledger.py:808-832 (_parse_acceptance) + SKILL.md:244 (--section "Acceptance") + adr-refine/SKILL.md:114-115 (template heading "## Definición de hecho")
survivors.scenario: adr-refine writes ACCEPTANCE.md with title `# Acceptance — <feature>` and checkbox section `## Definición de hecho`. dev-loop readiness is documented as `readiness --acceptance ACCEPTANCE.md --section "Acceptance"`. _parse_acceptance matches the TITLE line (contains 'acceptance') → in_scope=true, then the very next heading `## Definición de hecho` does NOT contain 'acceptance' → in_scope=false, so every real checkbox is skipped. Reproduced: same file returns (0,0) with --section Acceptance vs (1,2) with the real heading. total=0 → adr_dim=0.0, and since acceptance weight is 30 of ~100 (the single largest), readiness under-reports a fully-planned feature by up to 30 points with no error surfaced.
survivors.fix: Pick ONE canonical heading and make the template, the SKILL example, and a config default agree. Simplest: drop --section entirely from the readiness call (count the whole ACCEPTANCE.md) and remove the 'Out of scope' checkbox from the adr-refine template so it can't pollute the count. That deletes a whole class of silent mis-scoring.
survivors.fix_note: Part 1 of the fix (drop --section from the readiness call, count the whole ACCEPTANCE.md) is correct and minimal: it makes the documented invocation equal the already-correct CLI default (--section None → whole file), collapsing the entire mismatch class in one edit, and requires only aligning SKILL.md:243 and the usage string at qa_ledger.py:31. That is the essential fix and does NOT over-correct. Part 2 (remove the 'Out of scope' checkbox from the adr-refine template) is slightly speculative: the shipped template's Out-of-scope is already a plain bullet `- <límite>` (adr-refine/SKILL.md:121), not a checkbox, so there is nothing to pollute the whole-file count today — that part hardens against a future edit rather than fixing a live bug. It is low-cost and not ceremony, but strictly unnecessary for the current defect. Alternative equally-valid fix: keep --section but change the SKILL example and usage string to `--section "Definición de hecho"` (the actual checkbox heading), which scopes correctly and naturally excludes Out-of-scope. Either way, pick ONE canonical heading and make template + SKILL + usage string agree; the proposed 'drop --section' is the simplest and I'd take it.

survivors.title: Four of the sixteen subcommands (spec-check, pit-check, gate-check, golden-diff) are never invoked by the orchestrator that supposedly runs them — they exist only as prose in the CONSTITUTION
survivors.anchor: dev-loop/SKILL.md (grep for pit-check/gate-check/spec-check/golden-diff = zero hits across all 8 phases) vs qa_ledger.py:2089-2127 (the four parsers) and CONSTITUTION.md:89-101 (which claims each is 'enforced')
survivors.scenario: CONSTITUTION.md line 91-100 states simplicity/pit/gate/golden invariants are 'measured by qa_ledger.py <cmd>' and are BLOCKERs. But the dev-loop SKILL — the only thing that drives the loop — wires in exactly ONE of them (simplicity-check, Phase 2b). pit-check, gate-check, spec-check and golden-diff appear in NO phase. So on a normal run nobody executes them; the 'inviolable' gate-integrity/mutation/golden invariants are enforced only if a human remembers to run the command by hand. ~550 lines of the 2153-line engine (the four cmd_* + their regex tables + CLI wiring) are dead relative to the documented workflow.
survivors.fix: Either wire the four gates into explicit dev-loop phases (golden-diff before Phase 3, gate-check on every code-changing pass, spec-check in Phase 0, pit-check in Phase 5b) OR delete the subcommands and downgrade the CONSTITUTION clauses from 'enforced' to 'manual/aspirational'. Shipping a 2153-line engine where a quarter of the gates are unreachable from the orchestrator is the diamond: polished facets nobody's workflow touches.
survivors.fix_note: Over-corrects and adds ceremony. Forcing pit-check into Phase 5b 'every periodic run' contradicts CONSTITUTION.md:94's deliberate tiering out of the loop (mutation testing is expensive). Hardwiring golden-diff before Phase 3 unconditionally would misfire on greenfield dev-loop runs where no .approved corpus exists — golden-diff is migration-scoped (reverse-discovery flow), not every run. The 'delete the subcommands' alternative is worse: it guts the migration gate that characterize, reverse-discovery, and the PreToolUse hook all depend on. Minimal correct fix: add one gate-check --from-git invocation on code-changing passes in dev-loop Phase 2/3 (it reads facts, so it may block), and add spec-check to the discovery/adr-refine front-half. Leave pit-check (correctly tiered) and golden-diff (correctly migration-scoped) alone.

survivors.title: The method mandates 7-9 hand-authored markdown artifacts per change before code, with heavy overlap, and no lightweight tier — the ceremony scales with the doc count, not the problem
survivors.anchor: discovery/SKILL.md:83-101 (CONTEXT + CONSTITUTION + DOMAIN-MODEL + SPEC + ADR-per-decision + ACCEPTANCE + RISKS + HANDOFF) + CLAUDE.md template:11-12 ('If no SPEC.md + ACCEPTANCE.md, first model')
survivors.scenario: For any greenfield change, discovery writes CONTEXT.md, CONSTITUTION.md, DOMAIN-MODEL.md, SPEC.md, docs/adr/ADR-NNN.md, ACCEPTANCE.md, RISKS.md, HANDOFF.md. Several duplicate: SPEC.md already carries scope/out-of-scope/acceptance/rollback (discovery line 90), yet ACCEPTANCE.md re-states acceptance + out-of-scope, and HANDOFF.md re-states 'what to read + no-go rules' that CLAUDE.md already fixes permanently. CONTEXT (glossary) vs DOMAIN-MODEL (entities) is a real but fine distinction most changes won't need both of. There is no 'small change' path: the CLAUDE.md rule is absolute ('No codear desde una idea vaga').
survivors.fix: Collapse to a minimum viable spine: SPEC.md (with an Acceptance section and an Out-of-scope section inline) + docs/adr/ for genuinely hard-to-reverse decisions + CONSTITUTION.md for the project (written once, not per-change). Fold CONTEXT/DOMAIN-MODEL/RISKS/HANDOFF into SPEC sections that appear only when non-trivial. That keeps ~80% of the value (a testable acceptance list + recorded decisions + invariants) at ~40% of the authoring cost.
survivors.fix_note: The fix over-corrects and partly reinvents what exists. Its "minimum viable spine" (SPEC + inline Acceptance/Out-of-scope + ADR-for-hard-decisions + project-once CONSTITUTION) is essentially what /adr-refine already produces and what /discovery's lazy-write + sparing-ADR rules already permit — so it treats an existing lighter tier as missing. Worse, folding ACCEPTANCE into SPEC would break a working mechanism: qa_ledger.py readiness parses a standalone acceptance file by section (--acceptance/--section, lines 916/1156), so collapsing it regresses the gate. The only defensible trim is making HANDOFF.md conditional/dropped since CLAUDE.md:2-4 already fixes read-order and no-go rules permanently — a low-severity cleanup, not a structural redesign.

survivors.title: Nine CHANGELOG files (1.2.2–1.2.9) ship inside a kit whose config declares version 1.2.0 — accreted process artifacts the kit carries as payload
survivors.anchor: dev-loop-kit/ dir listing (CHANGELOG-1.2.2.md … CHANGELOG-1.2.9.md, README.md, WORKBENCH.md, workbench-doctor.sh) vs dev-loop.config.json:2 ("version": "1.2.0")
survivors.scenario: A consumer installing the kit gets nine per-patch changelog files plus WORKBENCH.md and workbench-doctor.sh as part of the deliverable, while the config still self-reports 1.2.0. The changelogs are meta-process about the kit's own evolution, not about the user's project; they add reading surface and version confusion at install time with no runtime value.
survivors.fix: Consolidate the nine CHANGELOG-1.2.x.md into a single CHANGELOG.md, sync the config version to the real release, and move workbench/doctor tooling out of the installed surface (or into a dev/ subdir). This is pure subtraction.
survivors.fix_note: The fix over-corrects and one part would regress the kit. Only the config-version sync is warranted, and since NO code reads the field (verified via rg over the whole kit), the minimal fix is to sync dev-loop.config.json:2 to 1.2.9 or delete the dead field entirely. The changelog consolidation is cosmetic taste (defensible, not required — the files aren't on the install read-path). The call to "move workbench/doctor tooling out of the installed surface" is wrong: README.md lines 214/217/244 treat WORKBENCH.md + workbench-doctor.sh as the canonical setup path, so removing them from the installed surface would strand documented commands — that is added breakage, not "pure subtraction" as claimed. The maker!=checker principle actually cuts the other way here: a facts-block/guesses-advise method would flag only the one verifiable inconsistency (config vs VERSION), not bundle in file-moves that break documented workflows.

survivors.title: `readiness` and `converged` re-walk every repo's entire source tree and re-parse JaCoCo/lcov on every invocation, and the skill tells operators to run readiness 'after ANY task' — a latency footgun on multi-repo runs.
survivors.anchor: qa_ledger.py:869-903 (_repo_readiness calls coverage()) + :925-931 (readiness re-loops coverage per repo) + count_loc/_test_file_set os.walk; SKILL.md:228 ('show this after finishing ANY task')
survivors.scenario: `cmd_readiness` calls `coverage(cfg.path, type)` once inside `_repo_readiness` for each repo (line 873) and AGAIN in the aggregate loop (lines 925-931) — coverage is globbed+parsed twice per repo per call. `coverage()` does a recursive glob over `**/target/**/jacoco.xml`; on a 5-repo config (this very config) with large `target/` trees that's 10 recursive filesystem walks per readiness call. Because the skill instructs showing readiness after every task, this runs constantly. On big monorepos this turns a 'quick KPI' into multi-second stalls, and operators start skipping it — killing the one number the method uses to communicate state.
survivors.fix: Read coverage from the last `snapshot` stored in the ledger instead of recomputing live (snapshots already persist coverage at qa_ledger.py:447-453), or at minimum compute each repo's coverage once and reuse it for both the per-repo and aggregate paths.
survivors.fix_note: The fix is half-sound. The "compute each repo's coverage once and reuse for per-repo and aggregate" half is clean and minimal: _repo_readiness already returns facts.coverage_pct (line 900) but the aggregate loop needs covered/missed (lines 929-930), so the minimal change is to also stash covered/missed in the returned dict and drop the second coverage() call — halves globs 10→5 with zero semantic change. The "read coverage from the last stored snapshot instead of recomputing live" half OVER-CORRECTS: snapshots (line 449) are only appended when cmd_snapshot runs explicitly, so a readiness KPI whose stated purpose is to "measure the STATE of the result" would report stale coverage from before recent code changes — trading a minor perf redundancy for a correctness/freshness regression on the one number the method uses to communicate state. Take the reuse half; reject the snapshot half.

survivors.title: Config default and skill text reference a QA tool named `improve-deep` that is not a real installed skill (the actual skill is `improve`), so a literal first-week setup mislogs or no-ops the third tool of every cycle.
survivors.anchor: dev-loop.config.json:15 (qa_tools_order: "improve-deep") + SKILL.md:122,126,130 + workbench-doctor.sh:32 (iterates both `improve` and `improve-deep`)
survivors.scenario: The available skill (per the environment's skill registry) is `improve`; `improve-deep` is not a skill name. A new operator following the config/SKILL literally will look for an `improve-deep` skill, not find it, and either skip the third tool (so cycles only ever run 2 of 3 tools while `tools-per-cycle` defaults to 3 — permanently NOT converged per _converged line 637) or log a `--tool improve-deep` step that never corresponds to a real pass. The doctor script hedging both names (workbench-doctor.sh:32) shows the ambiguity is known but unresolved in the shipped config.
survivors.fix: Standardize on the real skill name (`improve`) in `qa_tools_order`, SKILL.md, and the doctor script; if 'deep' is a mode, express it as an argument, not a distinct tool token that the ledger and convergence math treat as its own tool.
survivors.fix_note: The concrete action (standardize on `improve` across config line 15, SKILL.md 122/126/130, and drop the `improve-deep` hedge in workbench-doctor.sh:32) is correct, cheap, and adds no ceremony — a pure rename. But the fix's stated RATIONALE over-corrects: it claims "the ledger and convergence math treat [improve-deep] as its own tool," which is false. Neither the ledger (free-text `--tool`, no choices) nor `_converged` (name-agnostic count over agent steps) treats tokens as distinct tools. So the rename is worth doing purely for doc consistency/operator clarity, not because it repairs any convergence or logging defect — there is none to repair.

survivors.title: spec-check's untestable-criterion heuristic will fire on legitimate byte-equivalence specs and Rioplatense prose, and being advisory-by-default it gets ignored into noise.
survivors.anchor: qa_ledger.py:1745-1758 (_SC_VAGUE / _SC_MEASURABLE) + :1859-1866 (advisory unless --strict)
survivors.scenario: This very project's non-negotiable is 'salida byte-equivalente o funcionalmente idéntica' (project CLAUDE.md). `_SC_VAGUE` matches 'correcto/correcta' and 'idéntica'-adjacent phrasing while `_SC_MEASURABLE` only exempts a line if it also contains a comparator/number/'byte-equivalent'. Acceptance criteria written in normal Spanish ('el comportamiento es idéntico al de producción') get flagged as untestable even though they're the strongest possible criterion. Since spec-check is advisory unless `--strict`, the first few false flags train operators to ignore the whole SPEC-QUALITY block — so when it later flags a genuinely vague criterion, nobody reads it.
survivors.fix: Broaden `_SC_MEASURABLE` to recognize equivalence/golden phrasing ('idéntico a', 'igual que baseline', 'mismo CAE/PDF/hash') as measurable, and/or scope the vague-word list so common domain adjectives don't dominate the output; tune for signal so the advisory stays worth reading.
survivors.fix_note: The fix over-corrects and adds ceremony against a mostly-nonexistent problem. Adding 'idéntico a / igual que baseline / mismo CAE/PDF/hash' to _SC_MEASURABLE is largely redundant: those phrases already never flag because they contain no vague word (verified). Worse, whitelisting bare 'mismo'/'igual' as measurable would introduce real false NEGATIVES — e.g. 'es igual de rápido' or 'funciona igual de bien' would now be exempted despite being genuinely vague. The only real signal (the bare adjective 'correcto') is arguably a correct flag, so the only defensible micro-tune would be narrowing 'correcto/correcta' out of the vague list — but even that is optional since it advises, does not block, and points at a genuinely oracle-free word. No change is warranted.

survivors.title: The ledger's core convergence/readiness metrics are self-reported by the agent (the maker), not measured — directly violating 'metrics come from the ledger' and 'maker != checker'.
survivors.anchor: qa_ledger.py:497-531 (cmd_log_step) + :1987-1993 (CLI args) + :632-655 (_converged reads them)
survivors.scenario: Agent runs code-review, sees 4 HIGH findings, fixes 1, then calls `log-step --gated-reported 0 --fixed 4 --files-changed 0 --tests-passed true`. The ledger stores those integers verbatim (no cross-check against any tool output). `_converged` (line 640-648) sums `gated_reported`=0 and `files_changed`=0 over the last cycle and returns CONVERGED. `readiness` reports the loop closed. The maker fabricated the numbers the checker (ledger) then blessed. SKILL.md line 18-19 asserts 'All metrics come from the ledger — never estimate counts from memory' and the module docstring (:8-15) claims the ledger 'owns everything that MUST be exact' while explicitly delegating judgment to the skill — but the agent-tool findings ARE the memory-estimated counts, laundered through a CLI flag into a 'deterministic' record.
survivors.fix: Have the ledger ingest each agent tool's machine-readable output (as it already does for linters via `ingest-gate` diffing finding-IDs at :534-621) instead of accepting `--reported/--gated-reported/--fixed` as trusted scalars. At minimum require `--fingerprint` (finding IDs) on every agent `log-step` and compute `fixed` by set-diff against the prior pass, so the agent cannot assert a fix count the IDs don't support.
survivors.fix_note: The proposed fix over-corrects and manufactures false precision. The ledger ALREADY does exactly what the fix asks (finding-ID set-diff to compute 'fixed') for static linters via ingest-gate (:534-621) — because Checkstyle/PMD/SpotBugs emit stable, deterministic finding IDs. The two-category design (static-gate vs agent) exists precisely because the agent QA tools (code-review, judgment-day, improve) are LLM-driven and do NOT emit stable machine IDs. Mandating --fingerprint on every agent log-step and computing 'fixed' by set-diff over LLM findings would fabricate deterministic-looking counts out of inherently fuzzy output — the same 'false determinism' the claim objects to, relocated. --fingerprint is already correctly optional (:1994-1995) for oscillation detection when the agent can supply stable IDs. A proportionate improvement (not the proposed one) would be to have log-step distrust agent gated_reported=0 unless a fingerprint list is present, but even that adds ceremony to a 15%-weight advisory signal; the current split (measured caps guard the trusted agent numbers, human owns merge) is defensible as-is.

survivors.title: SKILL.md and config claim a CONSTITUTION breach is 'logged as a BLOCKER' that caps readiness ≤65 and blocks convergence 'by construction' — but the engine has no such mechanism; the word CONSTITUTION appears nowhere in it.
survivors.anchor: SKILL.md:238 (and :259-260, CONSTITUTION.md:11/88) vs qa_ledger.py (grep 'constitution|breach|invariant' → only a code comment at :1057)
survivors.scenario: Agent detects a change that breaches a CONSTITUTION invariant (e.g. a secret about to hit a log). Per the docs it should become a BLOCKER capping readiness ≤65. In reality the only ways severity_counts gets a BLOCKER/CRITICAL entry are the static linters via `ingest-gate` (:593-595, PMD priority-1→BLOCKER). `cmd_escalate` (:695-703) only appends to `ledger['escalations']`; that triggers the escalation cap (≤75) and ONLY when `not converged` (:892-893, :973-974). So a breach the agent 'logs' via escalate caps at 75, not 65 — and if the agent also reported a clean agent cycle, the escalation cap is skipped entirely and readiness is uncapped. The 'by construction' guarantee is prose, not code.
survivors.fix: Add a real ledger primitive, e.g. `qa_ledger.py flag-blocker --repo X --kind constitution --note ...` that writes a BLOCKER into the severity accounting so `_gate_open_and_sev`/`_apply_caps` actually enforce the ≤65 cap and `_converged` sees a non-clean gate. Until then, soften the SKILL/CONSTITUTION wording from 'by construction' to 'the agent must escalate' so the docs stop claiming an enforcement that does not exist.
survivors.fix_note: Sound and appropriately scoped, minor caveat. Ship the doc-softening half now (change "by construction" → "the agent must escalate") — it is the honest minimal correction. The `flag-blocker` primitive is the correct enforcement fix and reuses existing plumbing: it must write a static-gate-shaped record carrying both `severity_counts={"BLOCKER":1}` AND a nonzero `gated_reported`, so that `_gate_open_and_sev`/`_apply_caps` trip the ≤65 cap AND `_converged` sees a non-clean gate (otherwise it repeats the escalate half-fix that leaves convergence untouched). The `--kind constitution` label is a harmless note, not load-bearing; keep it a free-text note and do not grow a severity taxonomy. No real ceremony added — it is one subcommand mirroring the existing static-gate record shape.

survivors.title: The fact-based gates (gate-check, simplicity-check, pit-check, golden-diff) are pure exit-code tools that write nothing to the ledger and are wired into neither `converged` nor `readiness` — so 'facts may block' is only true if the agent voluntarily runs them and voluntarily obeys.
survivors.anchor: qa_ledger.py: cmd_gate_check :1652-1733, cmd_golden_diff :1904-1952, cmd_pit_check :1574-1616, cmd_simplicity_check :1466-1514 (all end in print+sys.exit, none call _save); _converged :632-655 and cmd_readiness :906-1022 reference only agent iterations + static-gate steps
survivors.scenario: Agent skips `golden-diff` (or runs it, sees DIVERGE/exit 1, and just proceeds). `converged` still returns 0 because it only inspects agent `log-step` records and `ingest-gate` static steps; readiness never reads a golden/mutation/gate-integrity result. A run with a diverged golden (the ONE fact the whole method is built around per CONSTITUTION.md:70-81 / characterize.md) can still report CONVERGED and a high readiness score. The 'facts block' invariant is enforced by agent goodwill, the same goodwill the method assumes is unreliable.
survivors.fix: Persist these gate verdicts to the ledger (a `log-gate` step) and make `_converged`/`readiness` refuse to converge / hard-cap when the latest golden-diff is DIVERGE, gate-check is BLOCKER, or pit-check is BELOW-GATE — mirroring how `_converged` already blocks on static-gate `gated_reported`. Right now the deterministic 'fact' gates have less binding power than the self-reported linter ingest.
survivors.fix_note: The fix is minimal and non-ceremonial because it MIRRORS machinery that already exists: _converged already blocks on static-gate gated_reported (632-655) and readiness already has a blocker_critical cap (970-972). Persisting a log-gate step and capping/blocking on latest golden-diff DIVERGE / gate-check BLOCKER / pit-check BELOW-GATE reuses that exact ledger-step + cap plumbing, adds no new abstraction layer, and closes the goodwill gap by construction. Two implementation cautions for downstream (not defects in the fix's direction): (1) reuse the existing cap/step mechanism rather than a parallel one to avoid duplicating the gate-integrity invariant the CONSTITUTION itself forbids; (2) golden-diff's 'no .received fixtures' path (1940-1942, exit 0) must be logged as 'not run', not as a passing gate, or an un-captured golden could mask a missing baseline.

survivors.title: `_tests_red` and the convergence 'tests green' condition trust the agent's `--tests-passed` flag rather than the parsed test report, so 'evidence captured, not narrated' is violated for the guardrail that stops the loop.
survivors.anchor: qa_ledger.py: _tests_red :846-856 (falls back to agent iteration `tests_passed`), _converged :642 `tests_ok = all(s.get('tests_passed') ...)`, cmd_log_step :517 sets it from `_to_bool(args.tests_passed)`
survivors.scenario: The suite is red, but the agent calls `log-step --tests-passed true`. `_converged` (:642) sees tests_ok=True. `_tests_red` (:851-855) only overrides via the snapshot path IF a fresh `snapshot` with a parsed surefire report exists AND shows failures; between snapshots it defers to the agent's boolean (:852-855), so the tests-red cap (≤35) never fires and the loop converges over a red suite. SKILL.md:27 ('A red suite stops the loop') and CLAUDE.md template rule 5 ('Evidencia capturada, no narrada … Ausente = sin evidencia, nunca OK') are both bypassed by a single mistyped/gamed flag.
survivors.fix: Derive `tests_passed` in `log-step` from a parsed Surefire/Failsafe (or flutter --machine) report the ledger reads itself — the maven_test_count parser at :170-193 already exists — instead of accepting a narrated boolean. `converged`'s tests check should read measured failures/errors, not the agent's word.
survivors.fix_note: The proposed fix over-corrects. Rewiring cmd_log_step to derive tests_passed from a parsed Surefire/Failsafe report couples every per-tool-pass log event (which also feeds churn/oscillation tracking) to repo path + freshly-regenerated reports matching that exact pass, and log-step is frequently called for passes that changed no code / ran no tests — adding ceremony and a fragile 'which report belongs to this pass' reconciliation. The minimal fix that matches the existing design: make _converged's tests_ok (:642) prefer the parsed snapshot's failures/errors when a snapshot exists — mirroring the precedence _tests_red ALREADY uses at :848-851 — falling back to the agent boolean only when no measured report is available. That reuses maven_test_count with zero new ceremony and closes the narrated-evidence gap for the advisory signal without touching log-step's contract. Given converged is advisory and Phase 5's post-snapshot already gates the PR factually, even this smaller fix is a nice-to-have hardening, not a critical correctness patch.

survivors.title: spec-check is advisory-by-default and explicitly disclaims the one thing that matters (consistency), leaving the SPEC's correctness entirely to a checker the method never guarantees is non-correlated.
survivors.anchor: qa_ledger.py cmd_spec_check :1841-1881 (`verdict = 'ADVISORY' if n_find else 'OK'`, `fail = args.strict and n_find>0`), _spec_check_text :1824-1830, and the printed line :1878 'consistencia: INFERENCIAL (checker no-correlacionado), no este lint'
survivors.scenario: A SPEC contains two contradictory acceptance criteria. spec-check runs, finds no vague words, prints OK (or ADVISORY, exit 0 without --strict), and the loop proceeds. The tool openly defers consistency to 'a non-correlated checker' (:1742-1744, :1878) — but nothing in dev-loop SKILL.md's Phase 0 (:49-60) requires that a second, non-correlated agent actually review the SPEC for contradictions. The 'maker != checker' rule is stated for the SPEC but never operationalized: the same agent that will build often is the only one that reads the SPEC.
survivors.fix: In dev-loop Phase 0, make the non-correlated SPEC consistency review a required, logged step (like judgment-day's blind dual review) before build, rather than leaving it as a comment the deterministic tool prints. Or run spec-check --strict as a real Phase-0 gate so at least the structural blockers block.
survivors.fix_note: Half-sound, half over-correcting. The FIRST half — make a non-correlated SPEC consistency review a required, logged Phase-0 step (mirroring judgment-day's blind dual review, but on the SPEC) — is the correct fix for the one genuine gap: it operationalizes the SPEC-side "maker != checker" the method only asserts. The SECOND half — "run spec-check --strict as a real Phase-0 gate so structural blockers block" — is the WRONG fix and over-corrects. --strict gates on heuristic/prose findings (vague words at :1824, missing out-of-scope, stack-naming at :1873-1875), NONE of which is consistency; only the two structural blockers (:1827-1830) are fact-based. Making the build block on prose heuristics is exactly the "guesses may block" inversion the method forbids (:1744) — it imports ceremony and false blocks (e.g. a criterion legitimately saying "robust" would block the build). The structural blockers alone (missing acceptance section / missing out-of-scope) could justify a hard gate, but that is not what the claim proposes, and it still would not address the consistency concern the finding is about. Net: adopt the dual-SPEC-review half; reject the --strict-gate half.

survivors.title: CWE-1074 is misapplied: the CONSTITUTION tags 'no speculative abstractions' with CWE-1074, but that CWE is officially 'Class with Excessively Deep Inheritance' — a different weakness a reader checking MITRE would catch.
survivors.anchor: templates/CONSTITUTION.md:42 (`<!-- CWE-1074 -->` on the 'Sin abstracciones especulativas' invariant)
survivors.scenario: A reviewer reads the CONSTITUTION invariant 'Sin abstracciones especulativas — cada tipo/capa nuevo se justifica contra la SPEC' mapped to CWE-1074, opens cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/1074.html expecting a match, and finds 'Class with Excessively Deep Inheritance' — which is about inheritance depth, not speculative/unrequested abstractions (YAGNI). The mapping is decorative, not accurate. This directly undercuts the doc's own stated principle that 'over-attributing lies': a CWE label that doesn't match the invariant is exactly an over-attribution that a checker would flag.
survivors.fix: Either drop the CWE tag on this line (speculative abstraction / YAGNI has no clean CWE), or if a code-quality CWE is wanted use one whose title actually matches (e.g. CWE-1048 'Invokable Control Element with Large Number of Outward Calls' is still a stretch; honest option is to remove it and label it 'YAGNI' as line 41 already does).
survivors.fix_note: The proposed fix (drop the CWE tag; do not force a stretch CWE like CWE-1048) is correct and minimal, with zero added ceremony: line 41 already labels the sibling YAGNI invariant with a plain "YAGNI / generalidad especulativa" comment and no CWE, so removing the tag matches existing style rather than inventing a new convention. Its restraint in refusing a stretch label is exactly right. The only under-scope: line 43's CWE-1121 (should be CWE-1124 or dropped) has the same defect and warrants the same treatment — an expansion of scope, not a flaw in the fix itself.

survivors.title: CWE-1121 is misapplied: 'bounded nesting / flatten with guard clauses' is tagged CWE-1121, but that CWE is 'Excessive McCabe Cyclomatic Complexity'; the correct one for nesting depth is CWE-1124 'Excessively Deep Nesting'.
survivors.anchor: templates/CONSTITUTION.md:43 (`<!-- CWE-1121 -->` on the 'Anidación acotada' invariant)
survivors.scenario: The invariant is 'Anidación acotada — aplanar con guard clauses / extraer función' (bounded nesting). It is tagged CWE-1121, which MITRE defines as 'Excessive McCabe Cyclomatic Complexity' — a related but distinct metric. The precise match for nesting depth is CWE-1124 ('Excessively Deep Nesting'), which I confirmed against MITRE. A reader who checks the citation finds the number points at cyclomatic complexity, not nesting.
survivors.fix: Change the tag on line 43 to `<!-- CWE-1124 -->` (Excessively Deep Nesting), which exactly matches the 'anidación acotada' invariant.
survivors.fix_note: Direction is correct — CWE-1124 exactly matches the "anidación acotada" invariant, and it adds no ceremony (a one-token swap). But as scoped the fix is incomplete: it only changes CONSTITUTION.md:43. The identical mis-tag appears in the gate engine at qa_ledger.py:1443 ("aplanar: guard clauses / extraer función (CWE-1121)"), which is the citation an operator actually sees in a finding. To be complete, both occurrences should become CWE-1124.

survivors.title: No artifact states the target user or the 'do NOT use this' boundary, so the method presents as universal — solo dev, team, greenfield, and migration all at once.
survivors.anchor: spec-loop-claude-code-doc-EN.html (hero: 'spec-loop: you bring the idea, the method builds the rest' — no audience line); dev-loop/SKILL.md:1-12 (description); templates/CLAUDE.md:9-34 (9 non-negotiable rules, no scope caveat)
survivors.scenario: A solo dev fixing a one-file bug reads the CLAUDE.md template's 9 innegotiable rules ('no codear desde una idea vaga: si no hay SPEC.md + ACCEPTANCE.md, primero /discovery o /adr-refine') and the dev-loop's 8-phase pipeline, and either (a) drags the full discovery→ADR→8-phase→sys-doc machine behind a trivial change, or (b) concludes the method is not for them and abandons it. The ONLY scoping guidance (risk profiles A–E) lives in the playbook play 03 and the long doc, never in the SKILL files the agent actually reads, and even there Profile A ('minor UI / config') still nominally enters the same CLAUDE.md rule set. The method never says in one place 'who this is for' or 'when a good prompt is cheaper'.
survivors.fix: Add a single 'Who this is for / when NOT to use it' block to dev-loop/SKILL.md and templates/CLAUDE.md (not just the playbook): name the primary user (e.g. 'one operator driving Claude Code on a non-trivial or risk-bearing change'), and state explicitly that Profile-A trivial changes SKIP discovery/ADR/sys-doc and run build+test only. Make the risk-profile tiering the FIRST decision in Phase 0, gating how much of the pipeline runs.
survivors.fix_note: The fix over-corrects and adds ceremony, which is itself a weakness by the method's own "converge, don't chase zero / simplicity" standard. Two problems: (1) It duplicates existing content. The "when NOT to use it" boundary already exists as a titled slide in the doc and as the A-E risk table in playbook play 03; adding another copy to two more files creates four places that must stay in sync — the method's own CLAUDE.md rule 2 ("la verdad vive en archivos") argues for ONE authoritative location, not scattering it. (2) "Make risk-profile tiering the FIRST decision in Phase 0, gating how much of the pipeline runs" mis-locates the gate. Risk classification is explicitly the front-half's job (play 03 is titled "Classify the change before you spend rigor on it," run by /discovery|/adr-refine), and dev-loop Phase 0 is documented as ADR-first — it consumes an ADR+ACCEPTANCE package that already encodes the risk decision. Forcing dev-loop to re-classify duplicates play 03 and contradicts the skill's stated contract ("If acceptance criteria are missing, stop and run adr-refine first"). The config already exposes the intended per-risk knob (config.defaults.simplicity, documented as "tighten per risk profile"), so the tiering hook exists where it belongs. A minimal, non-duplicative fix for the genuine residual gap would be a single one-line pointer in dev-loop/SKILL.md and templates/CLAUDE.md — e.g. "Scope first: trivial/throwaway/P0 work is out of scope; see play 03 risk profiles and the doc's 'When NOT to use it'" — linking to the existing authoritative sections rather than re-authoring a full block and re-architecting Phase 0.

survivors.title: The engine ships gate commands (spec-check, pit-check, gate-check, golden-diff) that the dev-loop SKILL never invokes — capability the CONSTITUTION promises but the actual loop the agent runs does not exercise.
survivors.anchor: qa_ledger.py has def cmd_spec_check, cmd_pit_check, cmd_gate_check, cmd_golden_diff (16 subcommands total); dev-loop/SKILL.md surfaces none of them (grep count 0 for spec-check/pit-check/golden-diff across the whole SKILL narrative)
survivors.scenario: The CONSTITUTION template says the Tests-efectivos invariant 'la mide qa_ledger.py pit-check', gate-integrity 'la mide qa_ledger.py gate-check', and golden 'la mide qa_ledger.py golden-diff'. But the dev-loop SKILL — the orchestration the agent actually follows — walks Phases 0–8 and never calls pit-check, gate-check, golden-diff, or spec-check. So an operator running /dev-loop as written enforces the simplicity gate (Phase 2b) but silently skips the mutation, gate-integrity, and golden invariants the CONSTITUTION declares BLOCKER-level. The method's own principle is 'facts may block'; here the fact-checkers exist in the engine but are never wired into the loop that claims them.
survivors.fix: Either wire pit-check/gate-check/golden-diff/spec-check into explicit dev-loop phases (golden-diff before judgment-day per the CONSTITUTION's own text; gate-check as part of every code-changing pass) with the risk-profile tiering, or remove those invariants from the CONSTITUTION template until the loop enforces them. Do not claim enforcement the runnable skill doesn't perform.
survivors.fix_note: The fix is directionally correct for the real gap but over-corrects on scope. Sound half: wire gate-check into every code-changing pass and golden-diff before judgment-day — this uses language the CONSTITUTION already contains (L99-100) and is minimal, not ceremony. Over-correction: demanding pit-check be wired into 'explicit dev-loop phases' contradicts the CONSTITUTION's own tiering (pit-check is deliberately scheduled/incremental, not inner-loop), and gating on spec-check would violate the method's 'guesses may only advise' principle since spec-check is ADVISORY by design. The alternative branch ('remove those invariants from the CONSTITUTION') also over-corrects — deleting real invariants to paper over a wiring gap. Minimal correct fix: add a Phase 3 gate-check step on code-changing passes and a golden-diff pre-judgment-day step (both already covenanted as BLOCKER); optionally add one line documenting WHERE pit-check runs (scheduled tier); leave spec-check advisory and unwired.

survivors.title: sys-doc's two-track CEO+technical HTML deck is a downstream deliverable that serves 'sell/present the system', not the core 'idea → verified build' loop — the clearest single instance of scope creep.
survivors.anchor: sys-doc/SKILL.md:14-79 (single self-contained HTML deck, dark control-room aesthetic, Commercial/CEO track + Technical track, inline SVG diagrams, print stylesheet, aria-labels); dev-loop/SKILL.md:248 ('Then invoke the sys-doc skill to generate the two-view HTML deck')
survivors.scenario: The method's purpose is turning an idea into a verified, merge-ready change. sys-doc instead produces a presentation artifact aimed at a CEO/commercial audience with control-room styling and slide navigation — a communication/marketing concern orthogonal to whether the code meets its SPEC. dev-loop Phase 8 hard-wires it into the mainline flow, so every full run is nudged toward generating a slide deck regardless of whether anyone needs one. The effort budget (a whole skill + build constraints for accessibility, print CSS, SVG theming) is disproportionate to the core loop.
survivors.fix: Move sys-doc out of the mandatory dev-loop Phase 8 into an explicitly optional 'reporting' add-on invoked only on request. Keep the ledger-driven retrospective (which IS evidence) in the core loop; make the two-track deck opt-in so the method's scope stays 'verified build', not 'verified build + stakeholder presentation'.
survivors.fix_note: The proposed fix is minimal and correct — arguably the model fix for a scope-creep finding. It deletes nothing (keeps sys-doc as an on-request add-on), preserves the evidence-bearing ledger retrospective in the core loop, and only adds an optionality guard to dev-loop:248. Critically it does NOT over-correct or add ceremony: it REMOVES ceremony from the mandatory path, and it reuses a convention already present in the same file (Phase 5b's explicit "(optional; ...)" marker at line 190), so it's a ~one-line, convention-consistent edit plus a description nudge. No new machinery, no new gate.
